claim: A delay-time byte does not scale a time and does not run a formula. It indexes a ladder of round decimal milliseconds whose step changes a few times over the byte, and every entry is then cut back to a whole step of a clock running at 32000 Hz -- which is what a delay addressed as a sample count does to a time written in milliseconds. Which ladder a slot is on is picked by the conversion column the effect list cites beside it, not by the range the page prints -- two slots print the same range and cite different columns, and they return ladders fifty milliseconds apart. On 0 - 500m the step is a tenth of a millisecond to setting fifty, then a half to sixty, then one to ninety, then ten to a hundred and sixteen, then twenty to a hundred and twenty-six; on 0 - 100m it is the same tenth to fifty and half to sixty, then one to a hundred, then two to a hundred and twenty-five; on 200m - 990m/1sec the byte starts at two hundred milliseconds and steps five to setting seventy, then ten to a hundred and fifteen, where it reaches one second; on 0m - 635m the step never changes at all -- five milliseconds from the first setting to the last; and 0m - 500m, which the page spells with an m the other five-hundred range does not have, is that range's ladder entry for entry. Four of the five reach the printed end before the byte ends and repeat it at every setting above, and the fifth reaches it at its last setting, so where a ladder stops is read off the record in both directions. The cut is not a detail of the ladder: it is what the settings at the short end actually return, and it is what decides which settings the reading brings back a tall peak for. It is also why two of the five ranges say nothing about the clock -- every entry on them is five milliseconds or more, which is already a whole step of it, so there is no setting at which the two readings differ. One slot of the five does not read its ladder from wherever it is asked. On the type whose delay glides, a setting reached from below is short of its cited column by a thousand and sixteen whole samples of the same clock, and the same setting reached from above returns that column times a hundred and twenty-seven over a hundred and twenty-eight exactly -- the same one-byte ratio every entry here carries. So the shortfall the sweep found is the sweep's own direction and not a second regime in the table, and the byte the page prints beside it as an acceleration is worth exactly half of it, from its top bit alone and from no other bit in the nibble. The ladder a column picks is the same ladder at every address that cites it. One type prints four of these rows at four addresses, three of which nothing in this class had been read at, and prints a different default against each -- 500ms, 300ms, 400ms, 200ms -- where the conversion column is one column for all four. All four return the ladder read on the type beside it, to within 0.042 ms at every setting either was asked at, against a floor of 0.0834 ms on the noisiest of them and 0.0 on the other three. So the printed default is not what picks a ladder either, which the page gives no other way to tell. A column's ladder does not change for what stands in front of the delay either. Four types that print this row put another stage before or beside it -- an enhancer, a chorus in front, a chorus beside, a flanger beside -- and every one of them returns the ladder its column was read on, to within 0.000 ms at all eight settings asked of each, on a reading quantised to 0.020833 ms. Two more print it behind a waveshaper and are not read here, for a reason that is about the reading and not about the byte.
whyNotNamed: The ladder is the claim and it is written out. A name for it would be a name for a table somebody laid out by hand, and there is nothing to call it but the numbers.
adds: The records say where the copy came back at each of the byte's hundred and twenty-eight settings, and how far each peak stood over the take's own roughness. What is read out of them here is that the times lie on a ladder of round steps, that the ladder is cut to a sample grid, which grid, and that the printed range picks which ladder. The grid does not come from the times at all: it comes from the peak heights, which no table of times can arrange, and it is arrived at separately on each of the two types read at every setting.
refutedBy: A reading at any setting of any of these slots that is not its range's ladder entry for it, by more than that setting's own resolution. Or a slot on another type one of these ranges is printed against whose ladder has different steps, which would make the printed range the wrong thing to index by. Or the same sweep on a unit whose delay is not clocked at 32000 Hz coming back with the heights split the same way, which would mean the split is not the grid.

values.why: The same chain with the part routed past the effect, which is what every reading below is taken against. It does two things and they are different. It is subtracted, so whatever the stimulus, the converters and the room put into a log spectrum is taken out of each reading rather than being read as a copy. And its own strongest peak is published, because a chain that puts a peak of its own somewhere is a chain that could hand a reading a delay the effect never made -- so a reader can see whether any setting landed near it. That peak is this curve before anything is taken off it, and near the bottom of the search it is the shape of the source itself, which sits there whatever is in the path. So it is not what says whether the chain would be read as a delay; the reading below is, because that is this curve put through the same subtraction every setting gets.
values.why_nothing_in_its_path: One take with the effect out, read as though it were a setting, against another take with the effect out as its control. That is the whole reading with the delay taken out of it, so what it returns is what a row has to stand over to be a delay rather than the chain, measured on this run's own stimulus instead of assumed from the bar. It is the sensitivity a negative needs: a bottom setting that returned nothing means nothing unless a take that certainly holds no copy also returns nothing here. Null where the run made only one such take, in which case there is no second one to read it against and the run measured no null.

eraPriors.claim: A delay line is addressed as a count of samples, so the times a byte selects are whole samples of whatever the part clocks at and not the round milliseconds a page prints.
eraPriors.why: A delay is a read pointer some distance behind a write pointer in a buffer, and that distance is an integer. Nothing in the era interpolates between two samples of a delay line to reach a printed millisecond; it would cost a multiply per sample to make a number on a page true.
eraPriors.wouldBeWrongIf: The times had come back on round milliseconds at the settings where a whole sample and a round millisecond disagree. 120 settings across the five ranges are such settings, and every one of them came back on the sample. They are all on the two ranges whose step falls under a millisecond: the other two never step finer than five milliseconds, which is a hundred and sixty whole steps of the clock, so neither has such a setting and neither is evidence here.

alternatives.reading: The ladder is in round milliseconds and the unit reaches them, so the 120 settings that came back short are the reading being short rather than the unit.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: The heights of the peaks. They split each byte's settings in two, and which side a setting falls on is predicted with nothing fitted by whether its time is a whole step of a clock at 32000 Hz. This candidate has no account of the split at all, and its own residual is further out than one setting's resolution at the shortest delay the slot makes -- on each of the records whose ladder steps finer than a whole step of the clock.

separatedBy.observable: The time at the settings where a whole sample and a round millisecond disagree, and the height of the peak there.

predicts.a-ladder-cut-to-whole-samples: no setting further out than that setting alone could be, on any of the five records
predicts.a-ladder-of-round-milliseconds: a setting further out than it could be on each record whose ladder steps finer than the clock, and no account of the heights at all

separatedBy.sensitivity_here: The settings a rate puts on the capture's own grid stand 2.522 spreads of the heights over the settings it does not, at 32000 Hz, against 1.608 for the next rate that predicts anything at all. A setting taken again moved 0.78 where the spread is 8.512. The other bytes read at every setting, on other types and other printed ranges, each name the same rate on their own: 01-40 puts 32000 Hz at 1.991 spreads against 1.519 for the next rate; 01-57 puts 32000 Hz at 2.411 spreads against 1.533 for the next rate.

alternatives.reading: The byte scales a time rather than indexing one -- a straight line or a run of equal ratios between the printed ends.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: The readings themselves, by whole octaves, on four of the five ranges. A straight line through the ends of 0 - 500m puts nothing under four milliseconds and the slot reaches a twelfth of one; a run of equal ratios reaches both ends and is wrong by more than an octave over most of what lies between, on every range including the one the line is right on.

separatedBy.observable: The time at every setting between the two ends.
separatedBy.sensitivity_here: The run resolved a setting taken four times onto one quefrency. The run of equal ratios is wrong by whole octaves over most of every byte read. The straight line is wrong by whole octaves over most of four of the five, and right at every setting of the fifth.

alternatives.reading: The range the page prints picks which ladder, which is what this claim said before the one slot that could tell the two apart was read.
alternatives.ruledOutBy: data/units/roland-sc8850-01/efx-time/01-54-03-the-ladder-nobody-read.json at settings 68 to 127, where the reading follows the cited column and stands thirteen per cent off the one the printed range would pick -- and by the page itself, which prints one range against two slots and cites a different column against each.

comparedAgainst.generatedFrom: Every record this class has, on every printed range it has one for. Five of the six are read at every setting the byte has, on five types and five ranges; the sixth is read at seven settings spanning three orders of magnitude and is there to answer whether two types printing one range share a ladder. Three of the swept bytes are the parameter the page numbers one and one is the parameter it numbers seventeen, which is the last stage of a chain of four.

domain.outside: How much of the output the returned copy is, which a cepstral peak does not weigh. What the other delay byte of a type does, which was parked for the whole run and not swept. Whether the ladder is the same on the rest of the class: the 5 ranges read here cover 54 of the class's 55 rows, and one slot of each range was read, so the claim is that the range picks the table and not that the other 1 rows were asked.

residual.why: The median is zero: the ladder returns the reading's own value at 552 of the 660 settings scored across the 6 records, and the rest are inside half a quefrency. The worst is at setting one, which is the shortest delay these slots make and the one the reading resolves worst -- half a quefrency is a fifth of an octave there. It is inside that setting's own floor. The swing above is reported against a single floor over the whole byte and it is the wrong yardstick here for the same reason: a byte covering three orders of magnitude has no one floor, which is why every setting is also counted against its own.

gates.name: gross
gates.why: The median residual over the span the byte commands. A rejection bound and not a target: below it the residual is reported and never optimised, because no candidate is decided by it.

gates.name: qualitative
gates.why: Every setting above the shortest the record admits is longer than it, in the unit and in the model alike. The byte is monotonic and so is the ladder.

figures.property: longer or shorter than the shortest setting the record admits

gates.name: power
gates.why: The strongest competing candidate is the same ladder without the cut, and it is not beaten on the residual alone -- it is contradicted by a reading it cannot produce. The heights of the peaks split the settings in two, and which side a setting falls on is predicted with nothing fitted by whether its time is a whole step of the clock. A table of times has no way to reach the height of a cepstral peak. The three bytes this can be read off are on three types and three printed ranges, and the scan names the same rate on each of them separately.

figures.why_not_every_record: Two of the five bytes read at every setting cannot name a rate and are not asked to. The scan works by which settings land on a quefrency the capture has and which fall between two, so a ladder whose every entry is already a whole step of the clock predicts every setting tall -- a prediction that cannot come out wrong. Both ranges that never step finer than five milliseconds are of that kind. Including them would add two records that agree with every rate equally.

gates.name: breakdown
gates.why: How many settings are further out than that setting alone could be, and by how much. The floors above are each one number over the whole byte, and this byte covers three orders of magnitude: half a quefrency is a fifth of an octave at its shortest setting and a ten-thousandth of one at its longest. A single floor is therefore far over the reading at one end and far under it at the other, so a candidate wrong where the reading is coarse passes it and a candidate right everywhere can fail it. This counts each setting against its own. It is reported beside the swing and does not replace it: the swing asks whether the residual leans, which is a different question from whether any one reading disagrees. One of the terms in it is not a quantisation at all: a delay is counted in the unit's clock and read in the one the take was captured on, so the whole reading is scaled by whatever those two sit apart, which is nothing at a tenth of a millisecond and more than a quefrency at a second. It is the same number of octaves everywhere and it is taken from the unit's own records, so a floor that left it out would be tighter than the rig at the long end and nowhere else.

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// delay-time
//
// Generated by yarn sync from inferences/models/time-a-ladder-cut-to-whole-samples.json.
// The claim it closes: inferences/roland-sc8850-01/time-the-byte-indexes-a-ladder-cut-to-whole-samples.json
//
// Every constant, every section count and every structural choice below is
// the model's. The difference equations are the ordinary realisations of the
// sections the model names — this site's arithmetic, not a measurement.
//
// Compared against the unit over:
//   01 50 40 03 03: all 128, and one of them four times
//   01 51 40 03 03: seven, and one of them four times
//   01 40 40 03 03: all 128, and one of them four times
//   01 52 40 03 03: all 128, and one of them four times
//   04 00 40 03 13: all 128, and one of them four times
//   01 57 40 03 03: all 128, and one of them four times
//   stimulus: channel 2, program 126, note 60, velocity 100, held 8.0 s, captured 9.0 s, 40 12 31 = 0
//
// Outside that domain this says nothing: How much of the output the returned copy is,
// which a cepstral peak does not weigh. What the other delay byte of a type does, which
// was parked for the whole run and not swept. Whether the ladder is the same on the rest
// of the class: the 5 ranges read here cover 54 of the class's 55 rows, and one slot of
// each range was read, so the claim is that the range picks the table and not that the
// other 1 rows were asked.
//
// Residual: 0 median, 0.1705 worst, in octaves.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

#include <cstring>

namespace soundings::delay_time {

// The same ladder with every entry cut back to a whole step of the rate the delay line
// counts in, which is what a delay written as a sample count does to a time written in
// milliseconds.

// printed range: 0 - 500m

/**
 * Which table applies is decided by the range the page prints against the
 * address, which is a fact about the document rather than about the byte.
 */
inline bool lookUp(const char* printedRange, int byte, double& out) {
  if (std::strcmp(printedRange, "0 - 500m") == 0) { out = at0500m(byte); return true; }
  if (std::strcmp(printedRange, "0 - 100m") == 0) { out = at0100m(byte); return true; }
  if (std::strcmp(printedRange, "200m - 990m/1sec") == 0) { out = at200m990m1sec(byte); return true; }
  if (std::strcmp(printedRange, "0m - 500m") == 0) { out = at0m500m(byte); return true; }
  if (std::strcmp(printedRange, "0m - 635m") == 0) { out = at0m635m(byte); return true; }
  // A range no reading has been taken over. Saying nothing is the answer:
  // returning a neighbouring table would be inventing a measurement.
  return false;
}

extra.key: a prediction that was made first
extra.text: The 0 - 100m ladder was written down and committed before the sweep that reads it, from the four settings the two ranges had already been seen to share and two further ones. It got the shape right and the breakpoint wrong: the prediction was a two-millisecond step from setting a hundred and four, and the unit changes step at a hundred. The error was in forcing the printed end onto the byte's last setting, when the longer range was already saturating two settings early and that had not been carried over. What survives is the part worth carrying to the four ranges still unread -- the step sizes transfer and the breakpoints do not, so a breakpoint is measured rather than solved for.

extra.key: a note on what was left out
extra.text: Nothing was left out by any record's own controls: every setting asked stood over the bar on all six records. One setting per record beginning at zero is left out of the comparison and not of the record, because a residual is a ratio and the winning candidate puts no time on one side of it there. Four runs' own nulls -- one take with the effect out read against another, which is this reading with the delay taken out of it -- came back under the bar, so the settings that did stand over it could have failed to. The longest range's null did not: it stands at thirteen times the roughness, at the stimulus's own repeat. That is named above rather than quietly passed, and what admits the run is that its weakest setting stands three times higher again and lands fifty quefrencies away.
